sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The window is not a smooth line: FY2019 operating income fell 58.9% to $5.5 billion on an 11.9pp margin drop, then FY2020 rebounded 186.2% to $15.7 billion [F13][F14][D97][D109][D148].

The FY2019 trough was an $8.3 billion impairment charge, including $6.8 billion of Shave Care goodwill, driven by currency devaluations, decelerating category growth and tougher US competition [X112][X109][P62].
Since FY2020 the top line has grown 2.0% a year to FY2026, with FY2025 the slowest year at 0.3% [D664][D406].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing 4.0pp of FY2020 growth and 2.2pp in FY2024, but only 0.1pp in FY2026 [D518][D530][D536].
In FY2026 the pattern flipped: non-US contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% revenue growth, with Beauty adding 1.3pp and Fabric & Home Care 0.8pp [D511][D457][D603][D543].
FY2026 sales rose on 2% favorable foreign exchange and 1% pricing with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at 4.1% against 3.3% a year [F202][F201].
Diluted EPS compounded at 1.9% against net income's 0.5%, helped by a share count that fell from 2,740.4 million to 2,422.5 million [F205][F203][X115][X124].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits 0.6pp above the window median of 22.1% and well above the FY2019 low of 8.1%, but below the FY2025 high of 24.3% [F30][D648][D646][D647].
The 1.6pp FY2026 decline came from a lower gross margin and higher marketing spending, with cost of revenue adding 1.0pp of drag and SG&A 0.6pp [D470][D483][D485][P25].
Gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix, partly offset by lower commodity costs and productivity savings [P5].
Net margin of 18.4% matched the window median, as a 20.8% tax rate and $1.1 billion of other income kept it close to operating margin [F50][D651][D443][X108].
Against staples peers, the FY2026 operating margin ranks in the 80th percentile versus a 14.3% median [D668][D669].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x, above the 0.87x staples peer median [F80][F40][D444][F100][D445][D679].
The 9.8% operating cash flow increase came from earnings and working capital, with payables generating $919 million offset by $641 million consumed by inventory [D462][P3].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% is near the 17.2% median but below the 20.5% FY2021 high [D441][D654][D653].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A, the highest capital intensity in the window [F90][D464][D440][D446].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, or 27.8% of revenue, with $9.9 billion of cash against $34.1 billion of total debt [D450][D451][F140][D449].
That leverage ranks in the 33rd percentile of six staples peers, whose median net cash is -1.0% of revenue [D676][D677].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026, down from 116.6% in FY2025 [X134][X144][D453][D402].
The current ratio of 0.68x is below the 0.72x window median, and working capital is negative $12.5 billion [F180][D663][F170].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x in every year of the window, reaching 0.68x in FY2026, so the shortfall is structural rather than new [F180][F171][R1].
For a company with this cash generation the negative working capital looks like a funding choice, not a liquidity stress [R1].
Payouts exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7%, funded partly by debt [D402][D453][R2].
Inventory days rose to 69 in FY2026 from 52 in FY2017, with $641 million of cash consumed by inventory in FY2026 [D455][D21][P3].
Operating margin: a FY2027 print below the 22.1% window median would confirm the FY2026 reversal, while a return above the 24.3% FY2025 high would restore the prior trend [D648][D647].
Free cash flow margin: a move below the 17.2% median would signal that rising capex is biting, given capex already reached 5.1% of revenue [D654][D440].
Payout cover: buybacks plus dividends above 100.7% of free cash flow again would extend the FY2025-FY2026 stretch [D453].

Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026, above the 1.02x window median, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x [F80][F40][D444][D660][F100][D445].
